domain: Workspace store (tenant runtime state) — src/lib/workspace.tsx, browser localStorage key `apragya.workspace`, STORAGE_VERSION 2. Every type below is persisted as one JSON blob in the visitor's browser only; there is no server, no tenant column, no user table, no referential integrity. All proposed SQL assumes each table gains `tenant_id uuid not null` plus `created_at/updated_at timestamptz`.

entities.name: Persisted
entities.purpose: The whole tenant workspace serialised to one localStorage string. Not exported, but it is the de-facto schema root: every collection field below becomes its own table.

fields.name: installed
fields.notes: App codes from marketApps ('CRM','HR'). Display/catalogue code string, not an FK.

fields.name: disabledApps
fields.notes: Second array keyed by the same app code; disabling is not uninstalling.

fields.name: creditsUsed
fields.notes: Single shared AI-credit counter. No ledger — only a running total, so spend cannot be attributed or reversed.

fields.name: twoFactor
fields.notes: Tenant-level flag; real 2FA is per-user.

fields.name: runs
fields.notes: Capped at 25 in memory (slice(0,25)); a DB must not inherit that cap.

fields.name: notifications
fields.notes: Capped at 50 (slice(0,50)).

fields.name: approvals
fields.sqlType: child table run_approval(approval_id text, decision text, decided_at timestamptz, decided_by uuid)
fields.notes: Map keyed by approval id with no decider, no timestamp, no note — the decision is the whole row today.

fields.name: audit
fields.notes: Append-only, newest first, truncated to 500 by logAudit.

fields.name: companies
fields.notes: Excludes the primary entity, which is derived from the session org name and never stored.

fields.name: primaryOverride
fields.sqlType: model the primary entity as a real company row instead
fields.notes: A sparse patch over a derived record. Unrepresentable as a column set; the primary company must become a first-class row.

fields.name: portalTabs
fields.sqlType: child table portal_tab(tab_key text, enabled boolean)
fields.notes: null is a sentinel meaning 'every tab on'; an empty array means 'all off'. Null vs empty carries opposite meaning — must not survive into SQL.

fields.name: dataInventory
fields.notes: Seeded from the platform catalogue in complianceData.ts, then tenant-editable — seed rows and tenant rows are indistinguishable.

fields.name: dataFlows
fields.notes: Same seed-vs-tenant ambiguity.

fields.name: kbCategories
fields.sqlType: child table kb_category(id uuid, name text)
fields.notes: Bare name strings; KbArticle.category points at one by name, not id.

fields.name: supportSettings
fields.sqlType: singleton row support_settings + several child tables

fields.name: pitchSampleLoaded
fields.notes: Demo-data flag. Should not exist in a production schema; sample rows need an `is_sample` column instead.

fields.name: appRecords
fields.notes: Untyped escape hatch keyed by surface string ('crm.leads','hr.employees'). Every CRM and HR record lives here with no schema at all.

fields.name: version
fields.notes: Absent on pre-v2 blobs; `stored.version ?? 1` is the migration hook.

relations.gap: No tenant_id anywhere. The blob IS the tenant, so a multi-tenant DB must add tenant_id to all ~50 tables and backfill it from the single workspace.

entities.name: Artifact
entities.purpose: A build output from Vibe Studio / the agent builder.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: crypto.randomUUID().

fields.name: skill
fields.notes: Free-text skill name, not an FK to any skill/agent catalogue row.

fields.name: kind
fields.notes: Unconstrained string — no enum exists for artifact kinds.

fields.name: version
fields.notes: Incremented on publish; there is no version history table, so older versions are lost.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.notes: ISO 8601 from new Date().toISOString().

relations.gap: Stored as a display name; no skill_id.

entities.name: Notification
entities.purpose: An in-product bell notification.

fields.name: body
fields.notes: Pre-rendered English sentence, not a template key + params — untranslatable and unlinkable.

fields.name: read
fields.notes: Per-tenant, not per-user; when real users exist this becomes notification_read(user_id, notification_id).

relations.gap: No recipient. Every notification is workspace-wide.
No resource_type/resource_id, so a notification cannot deep-link.

entities.name: Run
entities.purpose: One agent execution with its trace and credit cost.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: NOT a uuid today: `run_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,8)}` — 6 base-36 chars, collision-prone.

fields.name: agent
fields.sqlType: text not null (should be agent_id uuid)
fields.notes: Agent display name string.

fields.name: source
fields.notes: Where the run was triggered from; unconstrained.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: recordRun always writes 'success'; the other two are never produced.

fields.name: startedAt
fields.notes: No finishedAt — duration lives in `ms` instead.

fields.name: credits
fields.notes: Credits, not money — no currency. Summed from the trace.

fields.name: ms
fields.notes: Duration in milliseconds, summed from trace steps rather than measured.

fields.name: trace
fields.sqlType: child table run_step (or jsonb if steps are never queried)
fields.notes: Always the imported constant `sampleTrace` — every run shares the identical six steps.

relations.gap: Display name instead of agent_id.
Embedded array; needs run_step(run_id, seq).

entities.name: RunStep
entities.purpose: One node in an agent run's execution trace.

fields.name: detail
fields.notes: Pre-formatted human sentence including token counts; nothing is machine-readable.

relations.gap: No run_id and no sequence number; order is array position only.

entities.name: ApprovalDecision
entities.purpose: A reviewer's verdict on a paused human-in-the-loop run.

relations.gap: The approval queue itself is a static constant; only the decision is persisted, with no decider, timestamp, or modified payload. 'modified' has nowhere to store what was modified.

entities.name: AuditEvent
entities.purpose: One row of the tenant audit trail; written by nearly every mutator via auditEvent().

fields.name: user
fields.notes: Literal sentinel: 'owner' renders as the signed-in admin's email, '' means system. No actor id is ever recorded.

fields.name: role
fields.notes: Defaults to the literal 'Org_admin'; '' for system rows.

fields.name: action
fields.notes: Dotted verb ('app.installed','pos.invoice_created'). Some are built by interpolation (`asset.request_${status.toLowerCase()}`, `${key}.created`) so the vocabulary is open-ended and unenumerable.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Always 'Success' in practice — no mutator ever writes 'Failed'.

fields.name: resource
fields.notes: Resource type name; open string set.

fields.name: resourceId
fields.notes: Wildly inconsistent: sometimes a uuid, sometimes a reference ('SUP-0001'), sometimes an app code ('POS'), sometimes a person's name (pos.shift_opened writes shift.cashier), sometimes a sentence ('4 rows'). Defaults to a fresh random uuid pointing at nothing.

fields.name: ip
fields.notes: Always '' — a browser cannot see its own IP. Must be captured server-side.

relations.gap: No actor_user_id.
Untyped and inconsistent; not enforceable as an FK without normalising resourceId.

entities.name: Connection
entities.purpose: A configured link to an external system.

fields.name: connectorId
fields.notes: Catalogue slug from connectorData.ts, not a DB id.

fields.name: account
fields.notes: Account/tenant identifier at the far end, free text.

fields.name: secretHint
fields.notes: Last four characters of the credential. The real secret is deliberately never stored — a server schema needs a separate secret reference (vault key / KMS handle), which does not exist yet.

relations.gap: Points at a hardcoded TS catalogue, not a table.
No status, lastSyncAt, or error column — the row cannot say whether it works.

entities.name: CustomConnector
entities.purpose: A REST API the tenant registered itself.

fields.name: baseUrl
fields.notes: Unvalidated URL string.

fields.name: auth
fields.notes: Auth scheme label only; no credential storage.

fields.name: operations
fields.notes: A COUNT stored as a scalar — the operations themselves are never persisted, so the number cannot be verified or drilled into.

relations.gap: Needs a real child table; the count is currently the only evidence operations exist.

entities.name: Runner
entities.purpose: A self-hosted runner paired into the tenant's network.

fields.name: description
fields.notes: Typed non-null but written as '' when blank.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Only ever 'pending' — nothing transitions it, because no agent can call home to a localStorage store.

fields.name: token
fields.sqlType: text not null (store a hash, not the token)
fields.notes: Pairing secret generated in the browser as `apr_rnr_` + 24 hex chars. A real schema stores a hash + issued/expiry/consumed columns; a plaintext one-time secret must never be a persisted column.

fields.name: pairedAt
fields.notes: Misnamed: set at creation, before pairing actually happens. Needs createdAt + pairedAt + lastHeartbeatAt as three separate columns.

relations.gap: No lastSeenAt, version, or host columns.

entities.name: PosCustomer
entities.purpose: A trading partner in the Sales & POS master directory.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: The de-facto join key: PosDoc.customer stores this string.

fields.name: email
fields.notes: Typed non-null, written '' when blank; unvalidated.

fields.name: taxId
fields.notes: Free text. No jurisdiction/format column — do not assume any national tax-id scheme.

relations.gap: Customer groups exist in PosSettings but no customer row references one.
No billing or shipping address at all.

entities.name: PosDoc
entities.purpose: One order-to-cash document; `kind` decides which list it appears in.

fields.name: kind
fields.notes: Nine very different documents in one table; contract/subscription have no term or renewal columns at all.

fields.name: reference
fields.notes: Generated as `${prefix}-${(count of same kind)+1}` zero-padded to 4. Derived from array length, so deleting a document makes the next one reuse a reference. Needs a per-tenant per-kind sequence.

fields.name: customer
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING, not an FK. Renaming a customer orphans every document; a document can name a customer that was never created.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Unconstrained free string shared across all nine kinds — no per-kind state machine exists in the type.

fields.name: total
fields.notes: MONEY WITH NO CURRENCY COLUMN. The UI hardcodes 'USD' in pos/panes.tsx. Needs numeric(18,4) + currency char(3).

fields.name: source
fields.notes: Channel/origin label, free text.

fields.name: payment
fields.notes: Payment method/term label. No payment records, amounts paid, or settlement dates exist — a document cannot be partially paid.

fields.name: reason
fields.notes: Only meaningful for return/credit/refund; empty for the rest.

fields.name: dueDate
fields.notes: Date-only ('' when unset); compared as a string against today() in pos/panes.tsx. Not a timestamp.

relations.gap: Must become customer_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES pos_customer(id).
A sales document has no lines: no product, quantity, unit price, discount, or tax rows. `total` is a typed-in scalar with nothing behind it.
No quote→order→delivery→invoice chain; MatchSettings.requireOrder/requireDelivery gate a link that the schema cannot express.
Tax categories are configured but no document or line references one.

entities.name: PosShift
entities.purpose: A till session; closing it records the counted cash and its variance.

fields.name: cashier
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING, not an FK. Also used verbatim as the audit resourceId for pos.shift_opened.

fields.name: openingFloat
fields.notes: Money — pair with the row's `currency`.

fields.name: currency
fields.notes: The only money-bearing POS type that carries a currency; PosDoc and the variance thresholds do not.

fields.name: warehouse
fields.notes: Display-name string; no warehouse/location entity exists anywhere in the store.

fields.name: closedAt
fields.notes: Absent while the shift is open — the open/closed state is encoded only by this field's presence.

fields.name: cashTaken
fields.notes: Money. Initialised to 0 by openPosShift and NEVER incremented by any code path — no sale posts to a shift.

fields.name: cardTaken
fields.notes: Money. Same: always 0.

fields.name: countedCash
fields.notes: Money, set only at close. Variance is computed on the fly from openingFloat + cashTaken - countedCash and is not stored.

relations.gap: Needs cashier_user_id.
No shift_id on sales documents, so takings can never be reconciled to a shift.

entities.name: MatchSettings
entities.purpose: Three-way-match tolerances for POS posting.

fields.name: priceTolerance
fields.notes: A percentage (default 5), not money.

fields.name: priceAction
fields.notes: Stores the whole UI sentence: 'Warn — flag it, allow the post'. The enum value and its label are the same string, so changing copy breaks stored data.

fields.name: quantityTolerance
fields.notes: Percentage (default 2).

fields.name: quantityAction
fields.notes: Same sentence-as-enum problem.

entities.name: PosTaxCategory
entities.purpose: A named tax slab items point at instead of carrying a loose percentage.

fields.name: rate
fields.notes: Percentage, not money.

fields.name: withinState
fields.notes: Free-text component label. Its tax meaning is not defined anywhere in the code — see openQuestions; do not infer a statutory split.

fields.name: interState
fields.notes: Same: an uninterpreted label, no computation attached.

relations.gap: Nothing references a tax category; the comment says items point at one, but no item entity exists.

entities.name: PosCustomerGroup
entities.purpose: A customer segment configured in POS settings.

relations.gap: No membership column or join table — a group can never contain a customer.

entities.name: PosLoyaltyProgramme
entities.purpose: Points accrue on net subtotal and are spent at the till as a bill discount.

fields.name: pointsPer
fields.notes: Points earned per unit of spend — a ratio, not money.

fields.name: pointValue
fields.notes: MONEY per point, with no currency column.

fields.name: tiers
fields.sqlType: child table loyalty_tier(programme_id uuid, name text, threshold numeric(18,4), seq int)
fields.notes: Inline anonymous array. `threshold` is a money/points amount with no unit recorded — ambiguous which.

relations.gap: No ledger, balance, or accrual rows — points can be configured but never earned or spent.

entities.name: PosCashVariance
entities.purpose: Where a drawer count stops being silent and where the manager board colours.

fields.name: reasonAbove
fields.notes: MONEY (default 1) with no currency column — the code comment says 'in the till's own currency', which differs per shift, so a single tenant threshold is already ambiguous.

fields.name: amberWorst
fields.notes: Money, no currency.

fields.name: redWorst
fields.notes: Money, no currency.

fields.name: amberAverage
fields.notes: Money, no currency.

fields.name: redAverage
fields.notes: Money, no currency.

entities.name: PosCustomField
entities.purpose: A tenant-defined extra field on POS records.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Unconstrained string; no enum of supported field types, no required flag, no target entity, and no storage for the values themselves.

entities.name: PosChange
entities.purpose: One entry in the POS app's Change History, which is what makes a change undoable.

fields.name: by
fields.notes: Hardcoded literal 'owner' at the call site — never a real actor.

fields.name: summary
fields.notes: A one-line English sentence supplied by the caller. It is the ONLY record of what changed.

fields.name: reverted
fields.notes: Claims undoability, but no before/after payload is stored, so a revert is not reconstructible. Needs before_value/after_value jsonb.

entities.name: AppRecord
entities.purpose: One record captured by a generic create dialog (CRM leads, HR employees, etc.).

fields.name: title
fields.notes: Also used verbatim as the audit resourceId.

fields.name: fields
fields.notes: EVERY value is a string — dates, amounts, emails, booleans all collapse to text. CRM and HR have no real schema behind them, so this bag is the entire data model for those apps.

relations.gap: The owning surface is a map key, not a column; it must become surface_key text NOT NULL with an index.

entities.name: PosSettings
entities.purpose: Everything the Sales & POS settings tabs edit.

fields.name: agents
fields.tsType: { pauseAll: boolean; autoRunOnNew: boolean; autoPauseAt: string; disabled: string[] }
fields.sqlType: pause_all boolean, auto_run_on_new boolean, auto_pause_at ???, + child table pos_disabled_agent(agent_key text)
fields.notes: Inline anonymous object. `autoPauseAt` is a string with no documented format (time of day? credit threshold? date?) — see openQuestions. `disabled` holds agent key strings, not FKs.

entities.name: Rfp
entities.purpose: An inbound RFP on its way to becoming a pitch deck.

fields.name: prospect
fields.notes: Company name string; no prospect/account entity exists to point at.

fields.name: stage
fields.notes: Unconstrained string; the sample loader uses 'Your turn','Drafting','Out for client','Extracting' but no union type pins them down.

fields.name: vertical
fields.notes: Industry label, free text.

fields.name: estimate
fields.notes: MONEY WITH NO CURRENCY COLUMN (sample values 180000, 320000, 95000, 60000).

fields.name: schema
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING naming a CustomSchema ('Government / Municipal'), not its id. Renaming a schema orphans every RFP.

fields.name: deadline
fields.notes: Date-only; written as '' by the sample loader and the create form, never populated.

relations.gap: Must become schema_id uuid.
An RFP never links to the deck it produces.

entities.name: KbDoc
entities.purpose: A source document in the Pitch Pilot knowledge base.

fields.name: category
fields.notes: Free-text category name, not an FK.

relations.gap: No storage key, filename, size, MIME type, or extracted text — the 'document' is a title only. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.

entities.name: PitchTemplate
entities.purpose: A deck template; one per tenant can be the default.

fields.name: isDefault
fields.notes: First template added becomes default. Uniqueness needs a partial unique index (tenant_id) WHERE is_default.

relations.gap: No slides, layout, or file — a template is a name and a flag.

entities.name: BrandKit
entities.purpose: Firm identity applied to generated decks; defaults imported from pitchData.brandDefaults.

fields.name: firmName
fields.notes: Defaults to ''.

fields.name: logoUrl
fields.notes: A URL string; no upload/asset table behind it.

fields.name: primary
fields.notes: Hex colour, default '#1E3A8A'.

fields.name: accent
fields.notes: Default '#F59E0B'.

fields.name: dark
fields.notes: Default '#0F172A'.

fields.name: contactPhone
fields.notes: Free text, no country code or normalisation.

entities.name: CustomSchema
entities.purpose: A tenant-defined RFP extraction schema.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Rfp.schema stores this name, so it is a de-facto natural key and must be unique per tenant.

fields.name: fields
fields.sqlType: child table pitch_schema_field(schema_id uuid, label text, seq int)
fields.notes: Bare label strings — no type, no required flag, no extracted values stored anywhere.

relations.gap: Reverse link is by display name.

entities.name: Asset
entities.purpose: One individually tagged unit in the IT asset register.

fields.name: tagNo
fields.notes: Generated as taxonomy tagPrefix + (count of same-type assets + 1) padded to 4, falling back to 'AST-'. Derived from array length, so deleting an asset makes the next one reuse a tag. Needs a per-type sequence.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: TaxonomyEntry.value slug ('laptop'), looked up in assetSettings.taxonomies.asset_types. A slug FK, not a uuid.

fields.name: stage
fields.notes: Lifecycle stage as an unconstrained string; no union type defines the allowed stages.

fields.name: project
fields.notes: Display-name string; no project entity exists in the store.

fields.name: purchase
fields.notes: NOT the mode_of_purchase taxonomy despite the name overlap — the form placeholder is 'PO-1042', so it is a free-text purchase-order reference. The mode_of_purchase taxonomy is configured but nothing references it.

fields.name: assignedTo
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING or null. No assignment history table, so custody changes are invisible.

fields.name: warrantyEnd
fields.notes: From an <input type="date"> — date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD', '' when unset. daysUntil() parses it directly.

fields.name: acquiredAt
fields.notes: Set to the moment the row was created, NOT the real acquisition date — no purchase date, cost, depreciation, or supplier column exists anywhere.

relations.gap: Needs assigned_to_user_id uuid.
Needs project_id; no project table exists.
Slug reference into a JSON settings blob, not a table.

entities.name: AssetRequest
entities.purpose: A request raised against the asset register (new kit, support, retirement).

fields.name: reference
fields.notes: `REQ-` + (array length + 1) padded to 4 — same delete-and-reuse flaw.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Unconstrained request-type string.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Unconstrained; decideAssetRequest accepts any string and lowercases it into the audit action, so the status vocabulary is defined by call sites only.

fields.name: raisedBy
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING.

fields.name: approvedBy
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING or null. Set together with status but with no decided_at timestamp and no comment.

relations.gap: A request never references the asset it concerns.
Multi-level approval is configured in AssetSettings but a request stores a single approver name and no level.

entities.name: ApprovalLevel
entities.purpose: One rung of the asset-request approval ladder.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: Seeded as the literal 'l1', not a uuid.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Default 'By Role'; no union type enumerates the alternatives.

fields.name: approvers
fields.sqlType: child table approval_level_approver(level_id uuid, approver text)
fields.notes: Display-name strings — the seeded value is literally 'Manager (unknown)', a placeholder persisted as data.

entities.name: AssetSettings
entities.purpose: Everything the ITAM settings tab edits.

fields.name: customFields
fields.tsType: { id: string; label: string; type: string }[]
fields.notes: Inline anonymous shape, identical to PosCustomField but separately declared. No required flag, no value storage.

fields.name: taxonomies
fields.sqlType: child table asset_taxonomy(group_key text, value text, label text, tag_prefix text, seq int)
fields.notes: Nine fixed group keys seeded in `empty`: asset_types, makes, models, mode_of_purchase, retirement_reasons, warranty, numbering, reasons, notification. The key is a map key today and must become a column.

fields.name: agents
fields.tsType: { pauseAll: boolean; autoRunOnNew: boolean; autoPauseAt: string; disabled: string[] }
fields.sqlType: columns on asset_settings + child table asset_disabled_agent
fields.notes: Duplicate of the PosSettings.agents shape, declared inline in both places. `autoPauseAt` format undocumented.

entities.name: SupportRule
entities.purpose: A rule-shaped record in Support settings — escalations, inboxes, channels, business hours, auto-responses, shift handoffs, report schedules.

fields.name: detail
fields.notes: The ENTIRE rule body as one English sentence. Seven functionally different concepts (an IMAP inbox, a business-hours window, an SLA escalation, a report schedule) share this one shape, so none of them has the columns it actually needs — a mailbox has no host/port/credentials, a business-hours rule has no timezone or day/time columns, a report schedule has no cron or recipient.

relations.gap: The rule's kind is the name of the containing array; it must become rule_kind text NOT NULL.

entities.name: SupportSettings
entities.purpose: Everything the Support & Ticketing settings tab edits.

fields.name: statuses
fields.notes: Seeded from supportData.defaultStatuses.

fields.name: widget.confirmation
fields.notes: Default copy promises an email that nothing sends — see falseSuccessCopy.

fields.name: widget.accent
fields.notes: Default '#0f766e'.

fields.name: widget.position
fields.notes: Human label 'Bottom right' stored as the value.

fields.name: csat.lowScore
fields.notes: Threshold on Ticket.csat; the scale's bounds are never declared — see openQuestions.

fields.name: inboxAccounts
fields.notes: A mail account modelled as name + one sentence: no host, port, protocol, username, or secret reference.

fields.name: businessHours
fields.notes: No timezone, weekday, or open/close time columns.

fields.name: reportSchedules
fields.notes: No cadence or recipient columns.

fields.name: tierPolicies
fields.sqlType: child table support_tier_policy(tier text, policy_name text)
fields.notes: Tier name → SLA policy NAME. Both sides are display strings; no SLA policy entity exists at all. Empty means 'fall back to default'.

fields.name: indexedArticles
fields.notes: Array of KbArticle ids held on the settings object instead of a flag on the article.

entities.name: Ticket
entities.purpose: One support ticket.

fields.name: reference
fields.notes: `SUP-` + (tickets.length + 1) padded to 4 — reuses references after a delete.

fields.name: requester
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME/EMAIL STRING — no contact or user record behind it.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Should hold a FieldRow slug, but the type is a bare string with no constraint; a ticket can hold a status the tenant later deletes.

fields.name: priority
fields.notes: Same unconstrained slug reference. SLA hours live on the FieldRow, not the ticket.

fields.name: category
fields.notes: Same.

fields.name: source
fields.notes: Channel slug, unconstrained.

fields.name: tags
fields.sqlType: child table ticket_tag(ticket_id, tag text) or text[]

fields.name: assignee
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING or null. No team/queue column either.

fields.name: resolvedAt
fields.notes: Set on the first transition into a resolved state and then preserved (`item.resolvedAt ?? now`).

fields.name: slaBreached
fields.notes: A STORED flag, always written false at create, and no code ever flips it — no SLA due-date column exists to compute it from. Needs sla_due_at timestamptz and derivation.

fields.name: csat
fields.notes: Always null at create; no survey flow writes it. Scale bounds undeclared.

relations.gap: Needs assignee_user_id.
Needs requester_contact_id.
No messages, replies, notes, or attachments — a ticket is a header row with no body.
Tickets have no tier and no policy link.

entities.name: KbArticle
entities.purpose: A support knowledge-base article.

fields.name: category
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING matching an entry in Persisted.kbCategories, not an id.

fields.name: body
fields.notes: Format unknown — no markdown/html flag.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.notes: Only timestamp on the row; there is no createdAt, author, or revision history.

relations.gap: Category is a bare string in a string[] register.

entities.name: CannedResponse
entities.purpose: A reusable reply snippet for agents.

fields.name: body
fields.notes: No shortcut/keyword, no placeholder variables, no createdAt.

entities.name: TeSettings
entities.purpose: Travel & Expense configuration.

fields.name: receiptRequiredAbove
fields.notes: MONEY STORED AS A STRING, default ''. Empty string means 'no threshold', which a numeric column must express as NULL.

fields.name: categoryLimits
fields.sqlType: child table te_category_limit(category text, limit_amount numeric(18,4), currency char(3))
fields.notes: Category NAME → money-as-STRING. Both key and value need retyping.

fields.name: receiptEmail.address
fields.notes: Default 'expenses@apragya-tenant.mail' — a non-routable placeholder domain persisted as if it were a live inbox.

fields.name: travel.advancePercent
fields.notes: Percentage.

fields.name: travel.approvalAbove
fields.notes: MONEY AS STRING, default ''.

fields.name: travel.perDiem
fields.notes: MONEY AS STRING, default ''. No per-destination or per-grade dimension — a single flat value.

fields.name: travelNotifications
fields.sqlType: child table te_travel_notification(event_key text, enabled boolean)
fields.notes: Five seeded keys: submitted, approved, rejected, advance, settle. Map keys must become rows.

fields.name: approvalLevels
fields.tsType: { id: string; label: string; threshold: string }[]
fields.sqlType: child table te_approval_level(id uuid, seq int, label text, threshold_amount numeric(18,4), currency char(3))

fields.name: glAccounts

fields.notes: Category NAME → GL code string. No chart-of-accounts entity exists to validate against.

fields.name: customFields
fields.tsType: { id: string; label: string; type: string; required: boolean }[]

fields.name: segmentFields

fields.notes: Map of segment name → allowed values; both are free strings.

entities.name: ExpenseReport
entities.purpose: A trip's worth of expenses, submitted and reimbursed once.

fields.name: currency
fields.notes: One of only two money-bearing types in the file that carries a currency (with PosShift).

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Title-cased values used as stored data. advanceExpenseReport walks the array one step forward and clamps at the end — there is no reject/return path, so an approval cannot be refused.

fields.name: total
fields.notes: A typed-in scalar — there are no expense LINES anywhere in the store, so the total has nothing behind it and no receipt, category, date, or tax breakdown.

fields.name: reimbursedAt
fields.notes: Set when status reaches 'Reimbursed', from either advanceExpenseReport or a run disbursal.

relations.gap: An expense report has NO owner column at all — not even a name string. Who is being reimbursed is unrepresentable.
No child rows; `total` is the entire claim.
Who approved, and when, is never recorded.
A report cannot be linked to the trip it belongs to.

entities.name: TravelRequest
entities.purpose: A pre-trip travel authorisation.

fields.name: start
fields.notes: From <input type="date"> in travel/panes.tsx — date-only 'YYYY-MM-DD'. Reserved word; name the column start_date.

fields.name: end
fields.notes: Date-only. Reserved word; name it end_date. No CHECK (end_date >= start_date) exists anywhere.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: No origin or destination columns, so 'international' is an assertion, not a derivation.

fields.name: estimatedCost
fields.notes: MONEY WITH NO CURRENCY COLUMN, unlike ExpenseReport which has one.

fields.name: project
fields.notes: Display-name string; no project entity exists.

fields.name: budgetHead
fields.notes: Display-name string; no budget entity exists.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Only two states — no submitted/approved/rejected, despite TeSettings configuring travel approvals and advances.

relations.gap: No employee column — like ExpenseReport, the person is unrepresentable.
TeSettings.travel.advancePercent configures an advance with no row to record it on.

entities.name: CardTransaction
entities.purpose: A row imported from a corporate card statement CSV.

fields.name: date
fields.notes: Raw CSV cell, trimmed, never parsed or validated (travel/panes.tsx:305). Format is whatever the file contained.

fields.name: amount
fields.notes: MONEY WITH NO CURRENCY COLUMN. Parsed from CSV as a JS float.

fields.name: matchedTo
fields.notes: A real ExpenseReport.id — one of the few genuine id references in the file. Auto-matching picks the FIRST report whose total is within 0.005 of the amount, ignoring date and merchant, and the same report can be matched by several transactions (no uniqueness).

fields.name: —
fields.notes: No card, cardholder, statement batch, or import id — re-importing is deduped only by date|merchant|amount string equality.

relations.gap: Nullable, unenforced, and many-to-one in practice though the match is conceptually one-to-one.

entities.name: ReimbursementRun
entities.purpose: A batch that pays out a set of approved expense reports.

fields.name: stage
fields.notes: Typed as a bare string; the four stages exist only as a local array inside advanceReimbursementRun. Forward-only, clamped at 'Disbursed' — no failure or reversal stage.

fields.name: reportIds
fields.sqlType: join table reimbursement_run_report(run_id uuid, report_id uuid)
fields.notes: An array of FKs where a join table belongs — cannot be constrained, indexed, or carry a per-report paid amount.

fields.name: total
fields.notes: MONEY WITH NO CURRENCY COLUMN, summed across reports that may each carry a DIFFERENT currency — the sum is arithmetically wrong the moment two currencies are mixed.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.notes: No disbursedAt, no payment reference, no bank/batch file id.

relations.gap: Needs a join table.

entities.name: Dpia
entities.purpose: A Data Protection Impact Assessment record in the Compliance Center.

fields.name: activity
fields.notes: Free-text processing activity; not linked to DataFlow or InventoryField.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: No owner, reviewer, review date, or next-review date — a compliance register with no accountability columns.

relations.gap: The assessed processing is a sentence, not a reference.

entities.name: AutomatedDecision
entities.purpose: An automated decision / profiling activity register entry.

fields.name: humanReview
fields.notes: A claim recorded as a flag; nothing links it to the GuardrailPolicy 'hitl' machinery that would implement it.

relations.gap: The registered decision is a name only; it cannot point at the agent that makes it.

entities.name: RetentionPolicy
entities.purpose: How long data pulled through a connector is kept before purge.

fields.name: connectorId
fields.notes: Catalogue slug, not a Connection.id — the policy binds to a connector TYPE, so two connections of the same type cannot differ.

fields.name: lastRun
fields.notes: Always written '' at creation (ComplianceCenter.tsx:847) and never updated — no purge job exists. Empty string must become NULL.

entities.name: PortalPermission
entities.purpose: What a portal role may do on one tab.

fields.name: hidden
fields.sqlType: child table portal_role_hidden_field(role_id uuid, tab_key text, field_key text)
fields.notes: Field keys hidden from this role on this tab, as bare strings with no schema to validate against.

relations.gap: The tab it applies to is a map key; needs portal_role_permission(role_id, tab_key, ...).

entities.name: PortalRole
entities.purpose: A role a partner-portal user is assigned, deciding which tabs and fields they see.

fields.name: isDefault
fields.notes: Mutually exclusive per tenant (addPortalRole clears the flag on all others); needs a partial unique index.

fields.name: scope
fields.notes: Unconstrained scope string; no union defines the options.

fields.name: permissions
fields.sqlType: child table portal_role_permission(role_id, tab_key, read, comment, download)
fields.notes: Keyed by tab key string, which must match Persisted.portalTabs entries — no constraint links them.

relations.gap: No portal-user entity exists, so a role can never actually be assigned to anyone.

entities.name: GuardrailPolicy
entities.purpose: One guardrail policy gating agent inputs and outputs.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Seeded names carry the actual parameters in the text — 'Approval cap — ₹50,000', 'Max tool calls 8/12'. There is no threshold/limit column, so the rule's numbers exist only inside a display string and cannot be enforced.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Union from guardrailData.ts: Keyword Block | Content Filter | PII Redaction | Spend Cap | Rate Limit | Schema Validation. Stored as the human label, spaces and all.

fields.name: action
fields.notes: warn | block | redact | hitl.

fields.name: checkPoint
fields.notes: Input | Output | Both.

fields.name: scope
fields.notes: 'Global' or an installed app's code — a sentinel value mixed into what is otherwise an FK column.

relations.gap: 'Global' sentinel + app code in one text column; needs scope_kind + app_code.
Thresholds live in the display name; a real schema needs typed config (jsonb or per-type columns).

entities.name: Company
entities.purpose: A legal entity under the tenant.

fields.name: code
fields.notes: Uppercased in the form; no uniqueness is enforced today.

fields.name: currency
fields.notes: Free string in the type; the form defaults to 'USD'. The parent's currency is the reporting currency, but no FX rate table exists.

fields.name: country
fields.notes: Free string; no ISO constraint.

fields.name: parentId
fields.notes: Genuine self-referencing FK — one of the few in the file. No cycle check exists.

fields.name: status
fields.notes: Screaming-case, unlike every other status vocabulary in this file (Title Case or lower-case) — inconsistent conventions to reconcile before they become CHECK constraints.

fields.name: —
fields.notes: The PRIMARY entity is not a row at all: it is derived from the session org name and patched by Persisted.primaryOverride. A DB needs it as a real company row with is_primary.

relations.gap: Real id FK; needs ON DELETE handling and a cycle guard.

entities.name: IntercompanyPair
entities.purpose: Two entities that transact internally, and the account their postings net into.

fields.name: fromId
fields.notes: Real Company.id — a genuine FK. But the derived primary entity has no id, so it can never be one side of a pair.

fields.name: toId
fields.notes: No CHECK (fromId <> toId) and no uniqueness on the pair.

fields.name: eliminationAccount
fields.notes: A GL account code as free text; no chart-of-accounts table exists to reference.

relations.gap: Real ids; needs FKs plus a unique (tenant_id, fromId, toId).

entities.name: ScheduleKind
entities.purpose: What kind of thing a schedule runs.

entities.name: Schedule
entities.purpose: An agent, pipeline or bot running on a timer.

fields.name: target
fields.notes: DISPLAY NAME STRING of the agent/pipeline/bot to run — not an id, and not validated against any catalogue.

fields.name: cadence
fields.notes: Human label ('Hourly','Daily','Weekly','Monthly') used as the stored value. No cron expression and no timezone column, though nextRun() computes in UTC.

fields.name: nextRun
fields.notes: A PRE-FORMATTED HUMAN STRING, e.g. '22 Sep, 14:00 UTC' from toLocaleString('en-GB',…) in AdminScheduledJobs.tsx:32-50. Unsortable and unqueryable — must become a real timestamptz, with last_run_at and a separate display formatter.

fields.name: active
fields.notes: Toggling it does not recompute nextRun, so a reactivated schedule keeps a stale past due-time.

relations.gap: Polymorphic reference by display name; needs target_kind + target_id.

entities.name: ChecklistTask
entities.purpose: One onboarding-checklist row, recomputed from tenant state on every render.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: Hardcoded key, not stored.

fields.name: icon
fields.notes: An emoji literal held as content.

fields.name: done
fields.notes: Computed from artifacts.length / installed.length / three boolean flags. Only the underlying flags belong in the DB.

fields.name: to
fields.notes: An in-app route path baked into data.

entities.name: WorkspaceValue
entities.purpose: Persisted plus derived values and ~95 mutator functions; what useWorkspace() returns. Only the derived data fields are listed — the rest are callbacks, not columns.

fields.name: creditsTotal
fields.notes: Hardcoded module constant MONTHLY_CREDITS = 1000. Not per-tenant, not stored, not tied to a plan — a real schema needs a subscription/plan row.

fields.name: appQuota
fields.notes: Hardcoded APP_QUOTA = 5.

fields.name: trialDaysLeft
fields.notes: Hardcoded TRIAL_DAYS = 13 — a FROZEN number that never counts down, because no trial start/end date is stored anywhere.

entities.name: InventoryField
entities.sourceType: exported type alias (imported; persisted in Persisted.dataInventory)
entities.purpose: One catalogued personal-data field in the compliance inventory.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: Seed rows use `${entity}.${field}` as the id, not a uuid — so seeded and user-added rows have incompatible id formats in one column.

fields.name: entity
fields.notes: Physical table name string ('users','audit_logs'), unvalidated.

fields.name: field
fields.notes: Column name string. UNIQUE(tenant_id, entity, field) is implied by the seed id but not enforced.

fields.name: sensitive
fields.notes: Redundant with category='special_category' in the seed data but set independently, so the two can disagree.

fields.name: legalBasis
fields.notes: Free text ('Consent','Legitimate interests','Consent / Legitimate interests'). Not an enum, and the compound value shows why. Do not infer statutory meaning from these strings.

fields.name: retention
fields.notes: A human phrase, not a duration: 'Per KYC policy', '90 days (6y for PHI access)', 'Life of account + 730d post-erasure'. Unenforceable as written; a real schema needs a machine-readable interval plus this text as a note.

entities.name: DataFlow
entities.sourceType: exported type alias (imported; persisted in Persisted.dataFlows)
entities.purpose: One catalogued data movement in or out of the platform.

fields.name: id
fields.notes: Seed ids are slugified names ('ai-inference'), not uuids — same mixed-format problem as InventoryField.

fields.name: source
fields.notes: Free-text description, not a reference to a connector or system.

fields.name: destination
fields.notes: Free text, sometimes naming vendors ('Sentry','Object storage (MinIO/S3)').

fields.name: crossBorder
fields.notes: Transfer-safeguard label ('SCC + DPA') defaulting to ''. A legal classification held as free text — treat as a label, not an assertion.

entities.name: FieldRow
entities.sourceType: exported type alias (imported; persisted in SupportSettings)
entities.purpose: One configurable Support picklist entry (status, category, priority, type, channel).

fields.name: id
fields.notes: Seeded as the slug itself ('new','urgent').

fields.name: slug
fields.sqlType: text not null + UNIQUE(tenant_id, kind, slug)
fields.notes: What Ticket.status/priority/category/source should reference.

fields.name: color
fields.notes: A Tailwind palette key ('sky','rose') mapped through statusDot — presentation stored as data.

fields.name: behaviour
fields.notes: Only on statuses: 'active' | 'waiting' | 'closed'. Untyped in TS, so the closed-state semantics that drive resolvedAt are unconstrained.

fields.name: slaHours
fields.notes: Only on priorities (4/8/24/72). The SLA target lives here, not on the ticket, so changing a priority retroactively changes history.

fields.name: —
fields.notes: Which picklist a row belongs to is the containing array name; it must become a column.

entities.name: TaxonomyEntry
entities.sourceType: exported type alias (imported; persisted in AssetSettings.taxonomies)
entities.purpose: One entry in an ITAM master taxonomy.

fields.name: value
fields.sqlType: text not null + UNIQUE(tenant_id, group_key, value)
fields.notes: Slug; Asset.type references it. Note this type has NO id field — value is the key.

fields.name: tagPrefix
fields.notes: Drives Asset.tagNo generation ('LAP-'). Changing it mid-life silently renumbers nothing but changes future tags.

fields.name: configCount
fields.notes: A stored COUNT of configurations that are not themselves stored anywhere.

fields.name: —
fields.notes: The taxonomy group (asset_types, makes, …) is the Record key; it must become a column.

entities.name: GuardrailType / GuardrailAction / CheckPoint
entities.purpose: Guardrail vocabularies used by GuardrailPolicy.

entities.name: InventoryCategory / FlowType
entities.purpose: Compliance vocabularies used by InventoryField and DataFlow.

falseSuccessCopy.text: `${name} has been installed successfully. You can access it from the Enterprise sidebar.`
falseSuccessCopy.why: install() only pushes an app code string into a localStorage array. Nothing is provisioned, no schema or tenant data is created, and the word 'successfully' describes a browser-localStorage-only write.

falseSuccessCopy.text: `You ${decision} a paused run. The decision is recorded in the audit trail with actor and timestamp.`
falseSuccessCopy.why: Claims an actor is recorded. auditEvent() writes the literal string 'owner' as `user` and '' as `ip` — there is no actor id and no IP. The 'paused run' is a static constant in appData.ts, so nothing resumes, and a 'modified' decision has nowhere to store what was modified.

falseSuccessCopy.text: "Thanks — we've got your message and emailed you a copy."
falseSuccessCopy.why: Default support-widget confirmation promising an email. No mail is sent by anything in this store; the widget is a browser-localStorage-only config object.
A non-routable placeholder domain shipped as a real default inbox address. Enabling the toggle forwards nothing — no mail ingestion exists.

falseSuccessCopy.text: // Disbursing a run is what actually reimburses the reports inside it
falseSuccessCopy.why: advanceReimbursementRun() sets stage to 'Disbursed' and flips each ExpenseReport.status to 'Reimbursed' with a timestamp. No payment instruction, bank file, payment reference, or amount-paid is recorded — the word 'Disbursed' is a status string, and the reports have no claimant to pay in the first place.

falseSuccessCopy.text: // A pairing token is a one-time secret; this one is generated locally.
falseSuccessCopy.why: pairRunner() mints `apr_rnr_<24 hex>` in the browser and shows it as a pairing token. No server ever issued or can verify it, Runner.status is hardcoded 'pending' and nothing transitions it, so the pairing screen can never succeed.
The type comment says Change History 'is what makes a change undoable', but the row stores only an English `summary` — no before/after payload — so a revert cannot be reconstructed from the data.
Presented as an SLA breach indicator but hardcoded false at creation and never written again; no sla_due_at exists to derive it from. Any UI reading it reports 'within SLA' unconditionally.

falseSuccessCopy.text: /** Matches unmatched charges to reports of the same amount. Returns how many matched. */
falseSuccessCopy.why: autoMatchCards() matches on |report.total - txn.amount| < 0.005 alone — ignoring date, merchant and currency — takes the FIRST match, and lets many transactions match the same report. The returned count is reported to the user as successful reconciliation.
Seeded guardrails display concrete limits, but GuardrailPolicy has no threshold, limit or config column — the numbers exist only inside the display name and nothing can enforce them.

openQuestions: Tenancy: the entire store is a single browser-localStorage blob under key 'apragya.workspace'. Every one of the ~50 tables needs tenant_id added, plus a users table — today the only actor is the literal string 'owner'.

Money: 9 numeric money fields carry NO currency (PosDoc.total, Rfp.estimate, TravelRequest.estimatedCost, CardTransaction.amount, ReimbursementRun.total, all 5 PosCashVariance thresholds, PosLoyaltyProgramme.pointValue). Only ExpenseReport and PosShift have one. Is currency per-row, per-company (Company.currency), or a single tenant currency? ReimbursementRun.total sums reports that each carry their own currency — what is the intended behaviour when they differ, and is an FX rate table needed?

Money stored as text: TeSettings.receiptRequiredAbove, travel.approvalAbove, travel.perDiem, approvalLevels[].threshold and every value in categoryLimits are strings with '' meaning 'unset'. Confirm these become numeric(18,4) + currency with NULL for unset.

Credits: MONTHLY_CREDITS (1000), APP_QUOTA (5) and TRIAL_DAYS (13) are module constants, not tenant data. Should they become plan/subscription columns? Are credits integral or fractional (proposed numeric(18,4))? There is no credit ledger — only creditsUsed — so spend cannot be attributed, refunded, or reported per app/agent. Is a ledger table in scope?
Trial: trialDaysLeft is the frozen constant 13. A real schema needs trial_started_at / trial_ends_at. What is the trial length and what happens at expiry?

Expense and travel records have NO claimant/traveller column of any kind. Who owns an ExpenseReport and a TravelRequest, and against which employee entity? This is the single largest missing relation.
ExpenseReport has no line items, receipts, categories or per-line dates; `total` is a typed-in scalar. Are expense lines in scope, and what fields does a line carry?

Expense approval is forward-only (Draft → Submitted → Approved → Reimbursed, clamped). There is no reject, recall or return-for-edit path, and no approver or approved_at column. What is the real approval state machine?

PosDoc has no line items, no tax lines, no predecessor-document link and no payments. MatchSettings.requireOrder/requireDelivery gate a document chain the schema cannot express. What is the intended order-to-cash document graph?
PosTaxCategory.withinState / interState are uninterpreted labels with no computation attached anywhere. Their tax meaning must be specified by the product owner — do not infer any statutory split.
PosLoyaltyProgramme tier `threshold`: points or money? No accrual/balance storage exists; is a points ledger in scope?
PosShift.cashTaken and cardTaken are initialised to 0 and never incremented — no sale posts to a shift. Should sales documents carry shift_id so takings reconcile?

Reference generation: Ticket ('SUP-nnnn'), AssetRequest ('REQ-nnnn'), PosDoc (per-kind prefix) and Asset.tagNo all derive from array length + 1, so deleting a record makes the next one reuse a reference. Confirm these become per-tenant (and per-kind/per-type) database sequences, and whether existing references must be preserved.
Ticket.csat and SupportSettings.csat.lowScore: the scale's bounds are never declared (1-5? 1-10? 0-100?).
FieldRow.behaviour ('active'|'waiting'|'closed') drives whether a ticket counts as resolved but is typed as an optional bare string. Is it a required enum on statuses?
SLA: SupportSettings.tierPolicies maps a tier NAME to an SLA policy NAME, but no SLA policy entity and no ticket tier column exist. What is the SLA model?
AssetSettings.agents.autoPauseAt and PosSettings.agents.autoPauseAt are strings with no documented format — time of day, a date, or a credit threshold?

Asset.purchase holds a free-text PO reference ('PO-1042' placeholder) while a mode_of_purchase taxonomy is configured but referenced by nothing. Which is intended, and where do purchase date, cost, supplier and depreciation live? The asset register currently has no financial columns at all.
Asset.acquiredAt is set to row-creation time, not the real acquisition date. Should they be separate columns?

Schedule.nextRun is a pre-formatted display string ('22 Sep, 14:00 UTC') and cadence is a human label with no timezone column. Confirm nextRun becomes timestamptz, cadence becomes a cron expression or enum + a timezone, and add last_run_at.

Schedule.target, Run.agent, Artifact.skill and GuardrailPolicy.scope are all display-name strings for agents/pipelines/bots/apps. Where does the authoritative agent catalogue live, and what is its key?
GuardrailPolicy has no parameter storage — 'Approval cap — ₹50,000' and 'Max tool calls 8/12' keep their limits inside the name. What typed config does each GuardrailType need?
Persisted.approvals is a bare map of approvalId → decision. Where do the paused runs themselves live, who decided, when, and what payload did a 'modified' decision write?
Persisted.portalTabs uses null to mean 'all tabs enabled' and [] to mean 'none' — opposite meanings. Confirm the intended default before this becomes rows.
PortalRole has no portal-user entity to be assigned to. Are portal users in scope?

Company: the PRIMARY entity is not a row — it is derived from the session org name and patched by primaryOverride (a Partial<Company>). It must become a real row with is_primary; what backfills its code, currency and country?
Company.status is 'ACTIVE'/'INACTIVE' (screaming case) while every other status vocabulary in the file is Title Case or lower-case. Pick one convention before writing CHECK constraints.

InventoryField.retention holds human phrases ('Per KYC policy', '90 days (6y for PHI access)', 'Life of account + 730d post-erasure') that are not machine-readable, and legalBasis includes a compound value ('Consent / Legitimate interests'). These are compliance labels transcribed from a live console — they need product/legal sign-off before being turned into enforceable enums or intervals. Do not synthesise statutory meaning from them.
RetentionPolicy binds to a connector TYPE slug, not a Connection.id, and lastRun is always ''. Should policies be per-connection, and what job updates lastRun?
Connection stores only secretHint (last four chars); the real credential has no home. What secret store / vault reference column is expected?

Seed vs tenant data: dataInventory, dataFlows, supportSettings picklists, assetSettings taxonomies and defaultPolicies are all seeded from TS constants into the tenant blob with slug/composite ids, then edited in place. Seeded and user-created rows become indistinguishable and use different id formats. Should seeds be a separate catalogue table, or copied per tenant with an is_seed flag?

CRM and HR have no schema at all: every record goes into Persisted.appRecords[surfaceKey] as AppRecord with Record<string,string> fields. Real tables are needed — what are the CRM lead/contact/deal and HR employee schemas?
KbDoc, PitchTemplate and BrandKit.logoUrl imply file storage that does not exist (no storage key, filename, size, MIME type or extracted text). What is the file/blob model?

Custom fields are declared three separate times with three slightly different inline shapes (PosCustomField, AssetSettings.customFields, TeSettings.customFields — the last adds `required`), and none stores values. Should there be one custom-field system with typed values?
Notification has no recipient and no resource link; `read` is per-tenant. Confirm the per-user read model and deep-link columns.
Array caps baked into the store — notifications 50, runs 25, audit 500 — are UI conveniences. Confirm they are dropped in the DB and handled by pagination/retention instead.
